title: 独立证实电子衍射 (薄膜实验)
title_en: Independently Confirms Electron Diffraction (Thin Film Experiment)

video.title: 物理学史上最大的父子对决
video.title_en: The Biggest Battle in Physics between Father and Son

summary.text: 在戴维森和革末在美国进行实验的同时, 苏格兰阿伯丁大学的乔治·佩吉特·汤姆孙 (G.P. Thomson) 独立地设计了另一种实验来验证德布罗意的假说. 他将高速电子束穿过极薄的金属箔 (如金箔或铝箔, 而不是像戴维森那样从表面反射). 电子穿过金属箔后在后方的照相底片上形成了清晰的同心圆环 (衍射环). 这些圆环的直径与假设电子具有德布罗意波长 ($\lambda = h/p$) 时预测的X射线衍射图案完全一致. 这为电子的波动性提供了第二个独立的、无可辩驳的证据.
summary.text_en: While Davisson and Germer were experimenting in the US, George Paget Thomson (G.P. Thomson) at the University of Aberdeen in Scotland independently designed a different experiment to test de Broglie's hypothesis. He fired high-speed electrons *through* extremely thin metal foils (like gold or aluminum, rather than reflecting them off a surface). The electrons emerging from the foil formed sharp concentric rings (diffraction rings) on a photographic plate behind. These rings matched perfectly with the diffraction patterns predicted for waves of the de Broglie wavelength ($\lambda = h/p$). This provided a second, independent, and irrefutable proof of the wave nature of electrons.
key_points: 独立发现电子衍射 (Independent discovery of electron diffraction)
使用了透射法 (Transmission method) (穿过薄膜)
与戴维森 (Davisson) 共同获得1937年诺贝尔奖
key_points_en: Used the 'Transmission method' (passing through thin films)
Shared the 1937 Nobel Prize with Davisson

story.text: G.P. 汤姆孙的方法与戴维森不同, 他使用的是多晶薄膜. 因为薄膜中的微小晶体是随机排列的, 电子波被各个方向的晶格衍射, 最终在屏幕上形成了一系列明暗相间的圆环 (德拜-谢谢尔环). 这与X射线穿过同样薄膜产生的图案一模一样. 当他用磁场偏转这些圆环时, 圆环整体移动了, 证明这些"波"确实是由带电的电子组成的, 而不是光.
story.text_en: G.P. Thomson's method differed from Davisson's; he used polycrystalline thin films. Because the tiny crystals in the foil were randomly oriented, the electron waves were diffracted in all directions, creating a series of bright and dark concentric rings (Debye-Scherrer rings) on the screen. This pattern was identical to that produced by X-rays passing through the same foil. When he used a magnetic field to deflect the rings, they moved as a whole, proving these 'waves' were indeed made of charged electrons, not light.

fun_facts.text: 这是物理学史上最著名的家庭讽刺: 父亲 J.J. 汤姆孙 (`thomson_electron_1897`) 因证明电子是"粒子"而获得诺贝尔奖; 30年后, 他的儿子 G.P. 汤姆孙因证明电子是"波"而获得诺贝尔奖. 两人都是对的 (波粒二象性).
fun_facts.text_en: This is the most famous family irony in physics history: The father, J.J. Thomson (`thomson_electron_1897`), won the Nobel Prize for proving the electron is a *particle*. 30 years later, his son, G.P. Thomson, won the Nobel Prize for proving the electron is a *wave*. Both were right (wave-particle duality).

fun_facts.text: 除了物理学, G.P. 汤姆孙在二战期间还担任了英国"莫德委员会" (MAUD Committee) 的主席, 该委员会的报告直接促使美国启动了曼哈顿计划.
fun_facts.text_en: Beyond physics, during WWII, G.P. Thomson chaired the British 'MAUD Committee', whose report directly convinced the US to start the Manhattan Project.

simple_explanation.text:
戴维森是用电子去"撞墙" (反射), 看看它们怎么弹回来. 汤姆孙则是让电子"穿过窗帘" (透射薄膜).
如果你向窗帘喷水雾, 水雾穿过织物的微小缝隙后, 会散开形成特定的图案.
汤姆孙发现, 当电子穿过金箔时, 它们在底片上画出了一个个完美的圆圈. 只有波 (像涟漪一样) 穿过许多微小缝隙时才会形成这种圆圈. 如果电子只是子弹, 它们应该只会在中间留下一个点.
simple_explanation.text_en:
Davisson shot electrons *at a wall* (reflection) to see how they bounced. Thomson shot electrons *through a curtain* (transmission through thin film).
If you spray mist through the tiny gaps of a fabric, it spreads out into a specific pattern.
Thomson found that when electrons went through gold foil, they painted perfect *circles* on the film. Only waves (spreading like ripples) create these circles when passing through many tiny gaps. If electrons were just bullets, they would have just made a single dot in the middle.

applications.title: 透射电子显微镜 (TEM)
applications.text: 汤姆孙的实验装置实际上就是现代透射电子显微镜 (TEM) 的雏形. TEM利用电子穿透样品来获得原子级分辨率的图像.
applications.text_en: Thomson's experimental setup was effectively the prototype for the modern Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM), which uses electrons passing *through* a sample to image it at atomic resolution.

applications.title: 材料分析
applications.text: 电子衍射成为了分析晶体结构和薄膜材料性质的标准工具.
applications.text_en: Electron diffraction became a standard tool for analyzing crystal structures and the properties of thin film materials.

impact.text: G.P. 汤姆孙的发现与戴维森-革末实验互为补充, 彻底消除了对物质波假说的任何怀疑. 它证明了波粒二象性不依赖于特定的实验设置 (反射或透射), 而是电子本身固有的性质. 这一发现直接促成了量子力学的全面接受和电子显微镜技术的发展.
impact.text_en: G.P. Thomson's discovery complemented the Davisson-Germer experiment, removing any lingering doubts about the matter wave hypothesis. It proved that wave-particle duality didn't depend on a specific setup (reflection vs. transmission) but was an intrinsic property of the electron itself. This directly led to the universal acceptance of quantum mechanics and the development of electron microscopy.

influenced_by.contribution_en: J.J. Thomson (his father discovered the electron particle, providing the object for G.P.'s study)

influence_chain.legacy_text: 汤姆孙父子共同证明了电子的双重性格: 父亲证明它是粒子, 儿子证明它是波.
influence_chain.legacy_text_en: The Thomson father and son jointly proved the dual personality of the electron: the father proved it's a particle, the son proved it's a wave.

quiz.question: G.P. 汤姆孙的实验与戴维森-革末实验的主要区别是什么?
quiz.question_en: What was the main difference between G.P. Thomson's experiment and the Davisson-Germer experiment?
options: 汤姆孙使用了X射线, 戴维森使用了电子
汤姆孙让电子"穿过"薄膜 (透射), 戴维森让电子从晶体表面"反弹" (反射)
汤姆孙证明了电子是粒子, 戴维森证明了电子是波
汤姆孙使用了磁铁, 戴维森没有
options_en: Thomson used X-rays, Davisson used electrons
Thomson passed electrons *through* a film (transmission), Davisson *bounced* them off a crystal (reflection)
Thomson proved electrons are particles, Davisson proved they are waves
Thomson used magnets, Davisson did not
quiz.explanation: 虽然两者的结果都证明了电子的波动性 (衍射), 但实验几何结构不同. 戴维森观察的是单晶表面的反射衍射, 而汤姆孙观察的是穿过多晶薄膜的透射衍射 (类似于光穿过小孔).
quiz.explanation_en: While both results proved the wave nature of electrons (diffraction), the experimental geometry was different. Davisson observed reflection diffraction from a single crystal surface, while Thomson observed transmission diffraction through a polycrystalline film.
